A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Tensor Frames research. All 16 pages, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D, are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5-6 and Appendix D report original ModelNet40 regression and classification experiments, ablations, data-efficiency results, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1-3 and 7 and Figure 4.

M1.justification: Local-frame prediction, tensorial message passing, and the PointNet++ adaptation are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices B-C.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate normal-vector regression and classification on ModelNet40, retaining the same rotation/reflection scenarios and training-data coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Luo et al. and Table 2 retains CRIN. The data-augmentation and scalar-message comparators, together with the random-frame variants in supplementary comparisons, are unchanged.

E3.justification: The train/test split, 1,024-point inputs, normalization, transformation protocols, metrics, architectures, and 800-epoch training settings remain identical in Section 5 and Appendix D.

E4.justification: The frame/message ablation in Table 3, data-efficiency analysis in Figure 4, orthonormal-frame observations in Appendix B, and runtime comparison in Table 7 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report runtime standard deviations based on 10 loops over the test set in Table 7. Run information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are unchanged, including Tables 1-3 and 7 and Figure 4. The tensor-message model retains 0.86 normal-vector cosine similarity and 88.3% classification accuracy under the corresponding reported settings.

T1.justification: The representation definitions, equivariance arguments, and derivations in Sections 3-4 and Appendices A-C are identical; no mathematical correction or additional proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about general O(d)-equivariant message passing, adapting existing architectures, tensorial communication, and normal-regression performance.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of tensor-message benefits, the qualification that data augmentation can outperform built-in equivariance at some dataset sizes, and the computational-cost discussion.

D1.justification: Appendices B-D retain identical implementation details, hyperparameters, architecture specifications, hardware descriptions, training times, and dataset-access information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the cited works are unchanged. Bibliography entries shift between pages but none are added, removed, or substantively revised.

P1.justification: V2 inserts an Acknowledgments and Disclosure of Funding section after the conclusion, naming DFG and Klaus Tschira Stiftung support. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; the scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment slightly changes page 9 spacing and redistributes references across pages 9-12. Figures 1-4 and Tables 1-7 retain their content, formatting, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: V2 adds funding attribution on page 9, with accompanying reference reflow and an updated arXiv stamp. This modest disclosure addition leaves the scientific argument, evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information unchanged, yielding no meaningful overall quality difference.
